Re-appointment of Director

Re-appointment of Director
The Members at the Annual General Meetings (AGM) of the Company held on 12th August, 2020 and 11th August, 2023 had approved the re-appointment of Mrs. Rajashree Birla (DIN: 00022995) as director retiring by rotation and her continuation in office as a Non-Executive Director beyond the age of seventy five years.
Most recently she was named the recipient of the ‘Lal Bahadur Shastri Award for Excellence 2024’. At the G20 EMPOWER Meet in Ahmedabad, the ‘G20 EMPOWER Award for ‘Lifetime Achievement’ was conferred upon Mrs. Birla by Smt. Smriti Irani, the erstwhile Minister of Women and Child Development / Minority Affairs, Government of India. Furthermore, Mrs. Birla was named as an exemplar in Rotary International’s healthcare programmes by the Hon’ble President, Smt. Droupadi Murmu. Dear Shareholders,
Global Economy in 2025
The global economy maintained its trajectory through 2025 despite elevated tariffs, policy uncertainty, and geopolitical tensions. The impact of tariff measures was less severe than projections had suggested, and growth across major economies remained broadly stable.

The global economy maintained its trajectory through 2025 despite elevated tariffs, policy uncertainty, and geopolitical tensions. The impact of tariff measures was less severe than projections had suggested, and growth across major economies remained broadly stable.
In a global landscape defined by volatility, geopolitical tension, and accelerating technological change, FY 2025‑26 has been a milestone year for the Group. Our large manufacturing businesses have consolidated their leadership positions, our newer ventures are scaling with conviction, and our legacy consumer businesses are being reshaped for a new era of growth. Across this diverse portfolio, one force continues to anchor our progress— trust.
World trade expanded faster than anticipated in 2025, as demand for AI-driven capex offset the effects of trade policy uncertainty and higher tariffs. The volume of world merchandise trade grew by 4.6%, compared to a forecast of 2.4%. For the second consecutive year, Asian economies were the largest contributors to total world trade volume growth, accounting for 3.2 percentage points of the 4.6% total — or 71% of the overall increase.

Trust is often viewed as an intangible asset. In reality, it is one of the most consequential forms of capital an institution can possess. In periods of uncertainty, markets can turn volatile and competitive advantages can erode. Trust, however, compounds. It enables organisations to make long-term investments when others hesitate, to navigate disruption with credibility, and to emerge stronger from periods of change.
Trade in 2025 was also supported by investment in AI infrastructure, demand in emerging markets, fiscal and monetary expansion in advanced economies, and frontloading of imports in North America ahead of anticipated "reciprocal" tariffs from the United States. The outbreak of conflict in the Middle East on February 28, 2026, along with the partial closure of the Strait of Hormuz and damage to energy production facilities, introduced a supply shock to the global economy.

For a group such as ours, trust extends far beyond the relationship between a company and its customers. It is reflected in the confidence of shareholders who support long-term value creation, the commitment of employees who choose to build their careers with us, the faith of partners and suppliers who invest alongside us, and the confidence of communities and governments that see us as a responsible participant in economic progress. Each of these constituencies grants an institution something invaluable: the licence to grow.
India in FY 2025-26: Domestic demand carries the economy forward
Against a challenging global backdrop marked by US tariff escalations and mounting trade policy uncertainty, the Indian economy demonstrated remarkable resilience during FY 2025-26. Real GDP growth accelerated to 7.6%, up from 7.1% in FY 2024-25, cementing India's position as the fastest‑growing major economy globally.
This is particularly relevant at a time when businesses are being asked to do more than deliver financial performance. They are expected to navigate technological disruption, manage increasingly complex supply chains, create meaningful employment, steward natural resources responsibly and contribute to social progress. Meeting these expectations requires more than scale or strategy. It requires credibility built over years and, in many cases, decades.

This performance was underpinned by robust domestic demand, low inflation, and a broad pro-growth reform agenda. On the demand side, private consumption grew 7.7% year-on-year, supported by income tax reductions and rationalisation of GST rates.
The strength of our portfolio today reflects the cumulative effect of that credibility. It has allowed us to invest through cycles, pursue transformation with confidence and attract talent, capital, and partnerships that strengthen our competitive position.
Economic activity was broad-based. On the supply side, manufacturing gained momentum, driven by the automobile and fast-moving consumer goods sectors. The services sector benefited from demand in retail trade, hospitality, transportation, and real estate. India also made progress in containing inflation, with the headline rate averaging 2% in FY 2025-26, down from 4.7% the previous year.

The defining feature of the global and domestic economies in FY 2025-26 was resilience in the face of volatility. The global economy grew by 3.3% in 2025, as shifting trade policies and elevated geopolitical uncertainties were offset by hyperscale investments in artificial intelligence-led technologies, an accommodative monetary stance and fiscal support in major economies.
India is the second-largest cement producer globally, with cement demand expected to cross 620–630 MTPA by FY2029-30, driven by sustained infrastructure and housing demand.
Risks to global growth have escalated with the West Asia war. The damage to critical energy facilities and closure of the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted supply chains, impacted global trade and exacerbated inflationary risks.

Expansion of the wires and cables market
Infrastructure development remains a central pillar of India’s growth strategy. Sustained public investment in roads, railways, ports, airports, metro networks and industrial corridors, alongside flagship programmes such as the National Infrastructure Pipeline and PM Gati Shakti, is accelerating construction activity across the country. These initiatives are creating significant long-term demand for cement, positioning the sector as a critical enabler of national development.
The Indian wires and cables market, valued at USD 9.32 billion in 2024, is set for substantial growth and projected to reach USD 17.08 billion by 2032 at a CAGR of 7.94%. This surge is primarily fuelled by rapid urbanisation, infrastructure expansion and rising electrification across residential, commercial and industrial segments. Increasing investments in power transmission and distribution, renewable energy integration, metro rail networks, data centres and smart city infrastructure are driving the demand for high-quality electrical cables and wiring solutions. As construction activity expands, the wires and cables segment is emerging as a critical enabler of modern infrastructure, presenting significant opportunities for companies to expand into adjacent building material categories.

The Indian cement sector continues to witness rapid growth, driven by rapid urbanisation, sustained infrastructure investments, affordable housing initiatives and the development of industrial corridors. Construction activity has increased manifold on account of these factors and in FY 2025-26, industry volumes were projected to reach ~460-465 MMT, reporting approximately 6–7% year-on-year growth, after touching ~435 MMT cement production in FY 2025.1
Despite short-term demand fluctuations, fundamentals remain robust, supported by per capita cement consumption of ~324 kg in India, much below the global average of ~460 kg. At UltraTech, we continue to leverage our deep expertise and market understanding to develop proactive strategies for responding to evolving industry requirements.

Increasing per capita cement consumption
Rapid urbanisation
Housing demand
India’s urban population continues to expand rapidly, with over 35% of the population now living in urban areas, a figure expected to reach ~37-39% by 2030. This steady migration from rural to urban centres is driving the need for housing, transport networks, commercial spaces and civic infrastructure. As cities expand and new urban clusters emerge, the demand for cement and building materials is expected to remain structurally strong.
India’s per capita cement consumption of around ~324 kg remains significantly below the global average of about ~460 kg, indicating substantial headroom for future growth. As infrastructure development accelerates, urbanisation deepens and housing demand rises, cement usage is expected to increase steadily. As per EPA Municipal solid waste (https://www.epa.gov/ report-environment/wastes) are the third-largest source of human-related methane emissions in the U.S. Methane is one of several non-CO2 gases that contribute to global climate change. Methane gas is released as wastes decompose, and emissions are a function of the total amount and makeup of the wastes as well as management facility location, design, and practices. Gas emissions can be affected by recycling and changing product use. For example, increased recycling of municipal solid waste reduces the amount of waste sent to landfills while also conserving natural resources (e.g., timber, water, and minerals) and preventing pollution by reducing the need to collect new raw materials.

Carbon capture, utilisation and storage
Carbon capture, utilisation and storage
Cement production requires sustained high-temperature heat for clinker formation. Traditionally, this thermal energy has been generated through the combustion of fossil fuels such as coal and petcoke in kilns and calciners. We are piloting Coolbrook’s RotoDynamic Heater (RDH) technology to transition from fossil fuel–based thermal energy to electrified process heat, using renewable electricity to achieve the required temperatures and eliminate coal-based combustion.

We are advancing carbon capture, utilisation and storage solutions to address residual and hard-to-abate process emissions from clinker production. Through technology evaluation, pilot initiatives and strategic collaborations, we are exploring scalable pathways to capture and potentially utilise or permanently store CO₂, supporting the deep decarbonisation of our operations and long term Net- zero ambition.

UltraTech entered into a collaboration agreement with the Institute for Carbon Management (“ICM”) at the University of California, Los Angeles (“UCLA”) to pilot a groundbreaking new technology: the Zero Carbon Lime ("ZeroCAL"). The ICM has developed ZeroCAL technology to reduce carbon dioxide emissions from cement manufacturing. Employee survey
Employee satisfaction

Employee satisfaction
The third-party administered ABG VIBES survey assessed employee satisfaction, sense of purpose, well-being, leadership effectiveness and development opportunities. We achieved a 97% participation rate and a 95% engagement score, reflecting strong employee advocacy. Notably, 98% employees expressed pride in being part of the organisation, 91% indicated intent to continue, and 94% would recommend the organisation as a great place to work. Insights from the survey are translated into structured action plans at business and manager levels. To further strengthen inclusivity, we introduced a dedicated survey for last-mile workers, enabling more targeted and responsive engagement interventions.
Grievance redressal
Festival and cultural celebrations
An independent, third party-managed channel is available for employees to raise concerns in confidence. All matters are reviewed objectively and addressed in line with a zero- tolerance approach. Appropriate corrective actions, including disciplinary measures where required, are implemented to uphold high standards of conduct and maintain a respectful, fair and transparent workplace culture across the organisation.

Festival and cultural celebrations were organised to promote engagement, and to foster a vibrant workplace culture. Activities ranged from Holi, Secret Santa exchanges at Christmas and themed Halloween events to nine days of Navratri celebrations, featuring Garba, colleagues clad in traditional attire, lantern- making and festive cooking. These celebrations strengthened employee connection, encouraged collaboration and reinforced a strong sense of belonging.
Restructuring policies
In the event of restructuring or organisational changes, we ensure fair treatment of employees through consultation, appropriate notice and severance benefits in line with regulations. Where feasible, employees are supported through redeployment opportunities, reskilling or retraining initiatives, and career transition assistance.

Your Company has established clear science-based pathways to decarbonisation – targeting 27% reduction in Scope 1 emission intensity and 69% reduction in Scope 2 emission intensity by 2032, from a 2017 base year (validated by Science Based Targets initiative - SBTi). Your Company’s research and development (“R&D”) function continues to be a key enabler for the strategy to deliver low carbon growth, strengthen product differentiation, and enhance long term business resilience. The R&D agenda is anchored in three priorities: lowering the environmental footprint of cement and concrete; improving operational efficiency; and developing next generation construction materials. In addition to innovation, R&D provides continuous technical and analytical support across operations, enabling informed decision making and performance optimisation. This is supported by a strong in-house scientific base and collaborations with leading academic institutions and global platforms, including participation in the Global Cement and Concrete Association (“GCCA”) Innovandi network.
Your Company follows a rigorous and structured framework for evaluating product performance, durability, and environmental impact. New formulations are assessed through comprehensive laboratory testing and validated through field trials under varied operating conditions. Durability and long-term performance are evaluated using established methodologies, supported by advanced analytical techniques to ensure consistency and reliability. This approach ensures that sustainability improvements are achieved without compromising product quality, performance, or customer outcomes.

These partnerships support advancements in low carbon cement chemistry, alternative fuels, circular materials, and process optimisation, while also enabling the application of data driven diagnostics and advanced modelling tools to improve operational performance.

During the year, R&D efforts were focused on reducing clinker intensity and enhancing the utilisation of supplementary cementitious materials (“SCMs”) such as fly ash, slag, and limestone. Work on grinding optimisation, including the development of in-house grinding aid formulations and refined particle size distribution strategies, enabled higher clinker substitution while maintaining product performance. At the same time, research on multi-component cementitious systems and concrete formulations improved functional performance, workability, and durability, while supporting lower embodied carbon. These efforts also facilitated greater use of industrial by-products, reinforcing your Company’s focus on resource efficiency and circularity.
Your Company will continue to advance lower clinker cement systems, improve the performance of blended and composite cements, and evaluate future ready binder technologies. Through these initiatives, your Company is reinforcing its ability to deliver sustainable building materials while supporting long term growth and value creation for stakeholders.

Executive Summary
In compliance with Rule 8(3) of the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility) Rules, 2014, UltraTech Cement Limited (“UltraTech”) undertook Impact Assessment, through an independent agency, of the CSR Projects having outlays of one crore rupees or more, and which have been completed not less than a year before undertaking the study.
Improved educational environments through investments in government schools, Navodaya coaching centres (608 students preparing for entrance exams), green school solar energy projects (1,500 students benefited near Panipat), and 295 model Anganwadis nurturing early childhood development.

Improved educational environments through investments in government schools, Navodaya coaching centres (608 students preparing for entrance exams), green school solar energy projects (1,500 students benefited near Panipat), and 295 model Anganwadis nurturing early childhood development.
UltraTech’s CSR engagement spans 52 manufacturing locations across 16 states & 1 union territory in India, reaching out to 1.8 million beneficiaries in 507 villages. All projects are implemented under the aegis of the Aditya Birla Centre for Community Initiatives and Rural Development, employing a bottom-up, participatory approach. The projects were critically reviewed vis-à-vis six parameters: (a) relevance (b) coherence (c) effectiveness (d) efficiency (e) impact, and (f) sustainability.
Increased agricultural productivity through watershed management projects in collaboration with NABARD and ICRISAT, resulting in 30–40% yield improvements in Andhra Pradesh, adoption of high-yield ‘Pragati’ seeds yielding 15–25x higher turmeric output, and integrated farming initiatives across multiple states.

Spanning five focus areas - Education, Healthcare, Sustainable Livelihoods, Infrastructure Development and Social Empowerment - the programmes addressed critical needs such as quality schooling, access to medical services, clean water, enhanced public amenities, vocational training and women’s empowerment, aligned with multiple UN SDGs.
Improved access to primary healthcare through a fleet of 23 ambulances, 14 Company hospitals, mobile health camps reaching 1.61 lakh patients, and immunisation drives covering 1.22 lakh children. Project Ojaswani improved health outcomes for 120+ tribal girls near Maihar Cement, while Project Dhanvantari at Manikgarh impacted over 2,000 community members.
During FY 2023-24, the Company spent L 136 crore in CSR (up from H 116 crore in FY 2022-23 and H 96 crore in FY 2021-22), reflecting a steadily growing commitment to inclusive socio-economic development.
Water conservation efforts through 8 check dams, 22 deepened ponds, and 241 million cubic feet of water conserved, reaching 35,218 farmers. The Watershed Management Project at Bhogasamudram elevated groundwater levels and transformed barren land into cultivable territory, winning the CII National Award for Excellence in Water Management 2023.

Mr. K. C. Jhanwar is the Managing Director of UltraTech Cement Limited. He took over this role on 1st January, 2020. Mr. Jhanwar is a Chartered Accountant by profession.
Ms. Anita Ramachandran holds a Master’s Degree in Management Studies from Jamnalal Bajaj Institute of Management. She is a renowned Human Resource professional with deep knowledge and experience of about 40 years as a management consultant. She is also one of the first generation of women professionals to become an entrepreneur and run a highly successful HR consulting and services organisation.
Mr. Vivek Agrawal is Whole Time Director and Chief Marketing Officer at UltraTech Cement Limited. Having joined the Group in 1993, Mr. Agrawal has held significant roles in the flagship cement company of the Aditya Birla Group such as Zonal Head – Grey Cement South, Head Marketing – Birla White and Head – RMC Business. He took over as the CEO of the acquired UAE based entity, Star Cement Co LLC in 2010 and achieved turnaround. Before joining the Group, he has worked with Tata Motors.

Mr. K. K. Maheshwari is a proven leader with expertise in strategy and finance, a passion for building outstanding teams and a disciplined focus on innovation and excellence in operations. In a distinguished career spanning nearly five decades, of which 41 years have been with the Group, Mr. Maheshwari has held several key leadership roles, including that of steering the Group’s chemicals, international trading, pulp and fibre, textiles and cement business. Mr. Maheshwari is credited with steering the growth of each of the businesses towards a more competitive and sustainable model and has overseen various greenfield and brownfield expansions as well as strategic acquisitions in India and globally.
In a career spanning 45 years with the Group, Mr. Jhanwar has worked across finance, operations and general management roles in the Cement and Chemical Sectors. He has deep expertise in project management and business strategy, as well as significant experience in acquisitions & integration.
Ms. Ramachandran began her career with AF Ferguson & Co. [AFF] (the KPMG network Company in India then) in 1976 as the first woman consultant of the firm. In her 19 years stint with AFF she worked across various parts of the country and in a wide range of functional areas. She was a Director at the time of leaving the firm.

Mr. Agrawal took over his current role in 2013 as the Chief Marketing Officer of the Cement Business spanning across Sales, Marketing, Logistics, Ready Mix Concrete, Building Products Division, UltraTech Building Solutions, and UTEC— a contemporary phygital ecosystem.
Mr. Jhanwar is a well-respected industry leader and is recognised as the preeminent voice of the cement and building materials industry in India. He was the past President of CMA as well as Chairman of the National Council for Cement and Building Materials (NCBM). NCBM is the premier research institute for the sector and has been instituted by the Government of India. Mr. Jhanwar is also a member of the Development Council for Cement Industry, which has been constituted by the Government of India in 2021 to guide the development of the sector in a holistic manner. Mr. Jhanwar is also a recipient of India’s Best CEO’s award by Fortune magazine for three years in a row.
Having earlier served as Managing Director of Grasim Industries Ltd. and UltraTech Cement Ltd., he is presently Non-Executive Vice Chairman of UltraTech Cement, Chairman of Business Review Council of the Group, Director of Aditya Birla Management Corporation Pvt. Ltd., member of Board of Governors of Birla Institute of Technology and Science and mentors Aditya Birla Global Trading.

With a firm focus on building brands, at scale, Mr. Agrawal has led the team through 6 successful post-merger integrations transitioning regional brands into a unified Brand UltraTech as a National Champion. UltraTech named India’s 7th most valuable brand in Kantar BrandZ 2025 Rankings.
Ms. Ramachandran founded Cerebrus Consultants in 1995 to focus on HR advisory services, including organisation transformation. Her reputation and innovative work helped her build Cerebrus into a firm with national presence and the firm has worked with over 1,000 companies in South Asia. Ms. Ramachandran is known as an authority in reward management in the country.
Mr. Agrawal has spearheaded Ready Mix Concrete into a market-leading business, incubated Building Product Division (BPD) into the next growth engine and scaled UltraTech Building Solutions as a largest branded retail chain under building and construction space.

As the Chief Manufacturing Officer earlier and now as the Managing Director, Mr. Jhanwar has led the sustainability agenda for UltraTech. He has been an active advocate of the sustainability agenda through industry bodies like Global Cement & Concrete Association (GCCA), Cement Manufacturers Association (CMA), The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) among several others. Under his leadership, UltraTech has achieved key sustainability milestones like SBTi validation of its GHG emission reduction targets and adoption of Internal Carbon Price (ICP). Under his stewardship the Company has become both water positive and plastic negative in its operations. UltraTech has the distinction of being the first Company from India and the second in Asia to issue Sustainability linked Bonds (SLB), a resounding endorsement of the progress made by the Company on its sustainability agenda under his leadership.

She also works with several PE firms and start-ups to mentor them through their growth journey. Emphasis of Matter
We draw attention to Note 33(b) of the standalone financial statements, which refers to the orders dated 31 August 2016 (Penalty of ` 1,616.83 crores) and 19 January 2017 (Penalty of ` 68.30 crores) of the Competition Commission of India (‘CCI’) against which the Company (including the erstwhile UltraTech Nathdwara Cement Limited) had filed appeals. Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements
Report on the internal financial controls with reference to the aforesaid standalone financial statements under Clause (i) of Sub-section 3 of Section 143 of the Act

Report on the internal financial controls with reference to the aforesaid standalone financial statements under Clause (i) of Sub-section 3 of Section 143 of the Act
A company’s internal financial controls with reference to financial statements is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company’s internal financial controls with reference to financial statements include those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorisations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorised acquisition, use, or disposition of the company’s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.

(Referred to in paragraph 2(A)(f) under ‘Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements’ section of our report of even date)
Opinion
We have audited the internal financial controls with reference to financial statements of UltraTech Cement Limited (“the Company”) as of 31 March 2026 in conjunction with our audit of the standalone financial statements of the Company for the year ended on that date.
In our opinion, the Company has, in all material respects, adequate internal financial controls with reference to financial statements and such internal financial controls were operating effectively as at 31 March 2026, based on the internal financial controls with reference to financial statements criteria established by the Company considering the essential components of such internal controls stated in the Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (the “Guidance Note”).
Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements

Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements
Because of the inherent limitations of internal financial controls with reference to financial statements, including the possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud may occur and not be detected. Also, projections of any evaluation of the internal financial controls with reference to financial statements to future periods are subject to the risk that the internal financial controls with reference to financial statements may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.
Management’s and Board of Directors’ Responsibilities for Internal Financial Controls

Management’s and Board of Directors’ Responsibilities for Internal Financial Controls
The Company’s Management and the Board of Directors are responsible for establishing and maintaining internal financial controls based on the internal financial controls with reference to financial statements criteria established by the Company considering the essential components of internal control stated in the Guidance Note. These responsibilities include the design, implementation and maintenance of adequate internal financial controls that were operating effectively for ensuring the orderly and efficient conduct of its business, including adherence to the company’s policies, the safeguarding of its assets, the prevention and detection of frauds and errors, the accuracy and completeness of the accounting records, and the timely preparation of reliable financial information, as required under the Act.

A business combination involving entities or businesses under common control is a business combination in which all of the combining entities or businesses are ultimately controlled by the same party or parties both before and after the business combination and the control is not transitory. (I) Market Risk:

(I) Market Risk:
The Company’s activities expose it to market risk, liquidity risk and credit risk. The Company’s overall risk management focuses on the unpredictability of financial markets and seeks to minimise potential adverse effects on the financial performance of the Company. The Company uses derivative financial instruments, such as foreign exchange forward contracts, foreign currency option contracts, principal only swaps, cross currency swaps that are entered to hedge foreign currency risk exposure, interest rate swaps, coupon only swaps to hedge variable interest rate exposure and commodity fixed price swaps to hedge commodity price risks. Derivatives are used exclusively for hedging purposes and not as trading or speculative instruments.
Market risk is the risk of loss of future earnings, fair values or future cash flows that may result from a change in the price of a financial instrument. The value of a financial instrument may change as a result of changes in the interest rates, foreign currency exchange rates, commodity prices, equity prices and other market changes that affect market risk sensitive instruments. Market risk is attributable to all market risk sensitive financial instruments including investments and deposits, foreign currency receivables, payables and borrowings.

Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements

Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements
A company’s internal financial controls with reference to financial statements is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company’s internal financial controls with reference to financial statements include those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorisations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorised acquisition, use, or disposition of the company’s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.

Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements

Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements
Because of the inherent limitations of internal financial controls with reference to financial statements, including the possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud may occur and not be detected. Also, projections of any evaluation of the internal financial controls with reference to financial statements to future periods are subject to the risk that the internal financial controls with reference to financial statements may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.

B) Interest rate risk:
I) Market Risk:

I) Market Risk:
Interest rate risk is the risk that the fair value or future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate because of changes in market interest rates. The Group’s exposure to the risk of changes in market interest rates relates primarily to the Group’s short term borrowing (excluding commercial paper) with floating interest rates. For all long-term borrowings with floating rates, the risk of variation in the interest rates is mitigated through interest rate swaps. The Group constantly monitors the credit markets and rebalances its financing strategies to achieve an optimal maturity profile and financing cost.
Market risk is the risk of loss of future earnings, fair values or future cash flows that may result from a change in the price of a financial instrument. The value of a financial instrument may change as a result of changes in the interest rates, foreign currency exchange rates, commodity prices, equity prices and other market changes that affect market risk sensitive instruments. Market risk is attributable to all market risk sensitive financial instruments including investments and deposits, foreign currency receivables, payables and borrowings.
A) Foreign Currency Risk:

A) Foreign Currency Risk:
Foreign currency risk is the risk of impact related to fair value or future cash flows of an exposure in foreign currency, which fluctuate due to changes in foreign exchange rates. The Group’s exposure to the risk of changes in foreign exchange rates relates primarily to the foreign currency borrowings, import of fuels, raw materials & spare parts, capital expenditure, exports of cement and the Company’s net investments in foreign subsidiaries.

The assurance engagement was planned and performed in accordance with the verification methodology developed by the TÜV SÜD Group, which is based upon ISAE 3000 and ISO 17029. For greenhouse gas-related disclosures, relevant principles of ISAE 3410 were also considered, where applicable. The engagement applied a reasonable assurance level for BRSR Core Indicators and a limited assurance level for selected sustainability indicators and claims disclosed in the Integrated and Sustainability Report. The verification was based on a systematic and evidence-based assurance process limited to the scope stated above. The selection of assurance procedures was subject to the verifier’s professional judgement. The procedures performed included, amongst others:

 Review of the reporting boundary, scope of reporting and applicable reporting criteria;  Inquiries with personnel responsible for sustainability reporting, data collection, consolidation and internal review;  Evaluation of the design and implementation of systems and processes for compiling, analysing and aggregating sustainability information;  Review of the Company’s data collection, collation and calculation methodologies;  Assessment of the appropriateness of quantification methods used for the BRSR Core Indicators and selected IR indicators;  Review of consistency of data and information within the Report and between the Report and source records;  Analytical review and inspection of selected sustainability information reported at corporate and site levels;  Execution of audit trail for selected claims and data streams to assess accuracy in collection, transcription and aggregation;  Assessment of internal controls relevant to sustainability data management and reporting;  Review of supporting documentation and evidence on a sample basis; and  Onsite and/or offsite verification at selected locations.
Introduction and objective of the engagement

Introduction and objective of the engagement
UltraTech Cement Limited (the 'Company') has developed its Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report FY 2025-26 (‘BRSR’) including the BRSR Core Indicators, based on the BRSR reporting guidelines prescribed by SEBI for listed entities. The reporting criteria have been derived from the Principles of National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct, 2018 (NGRBC), Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol - A Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard, and Global Cement and Concrete Association's Cement CO2 and Energy Protocol, Version 3.1. The Company has also developed its Integrated and Sustainability Report FY 2025-26 (‘IR’) based on the principles of the Integrated Reporting (<IR>) Framework published by the International Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC) and with reference to the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards. The BRSR would form a part of the IR. TÜV SÜD South Asia Pvt. Atul Daga: Hi. Good afternoon, good evening, everybody. Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for joining our
second quarter '27 earnings call. The September quarter is always the one where monsoon writes
part of the script. This year, it brought a different twist, a weak monsoon that kept construction
going alongside a West Asia conflict that flared up again and pushed fuel costs higher.
Time and again, we keep hearing chatter about cement prices, which is on everybody's mind,
and that's where I want to start first. In a normal year, cement prices slip during July and August
as rains slows sites and dealers chase volumes. This year, the industry largely avoided that. Pan-
India, average trade prices for Q2 were stable in line with Q1, with the quarterly average 1%,
1.5% lower, mainly because of a soft August. In the second half of September, prices turned
firmly upwards. Trade prices must have risen 7 to 10 per bag month-on-month and non-trade
prices even higher. We exited September in trade at least about 3% above the Q1 average. The
quarterly average is weighed down by a soft August. The run rate we take into Q3 is materially
better. One more thing I want to clarify here for ourselves, UltraTech. We take a view on price
changes with demand and macroeconomic trends. It's not a rocket science. If demand overshoots

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · DHIRAJ KAPOOR
chunks.text:
changes with demand and macroeconomic trends. It's not a rocket science. If demand overshoots
supply, it leads to price improvements. If there is a structural change in cost for the industry,
ultimately, the end customers will have to bear the cost. Given the spread of the industry in the
country, prices rise always with a lag to catch up on costs. This is nothing new. This is an age-
old phenomenon.
As for UltraTech, despite increase in cost, the company has achieved an improvement in
operating performance, higher capacity utilization on a higher base, higher or stable realizations,
improvement in efficiency and a 21% increase in net profit. Prices for your benefit have risen
substantially in the month of October and continue to stay high. My sense is that there is more
price improvement that will happen in the near future, in the next couple of months, that is to
say.
If you were to split the realizations by zone for the quarter, West, the prices were steady through
July and August, stepped up in September with Mumbai being the biggest market moving
strongly up by 3% to 4% per bag for both bag and bulk. Rest of Maharashtra, small dip in August
was followed by a big increase in September. Eastern markets, rains disruption pushed prices
down during August, but we have seen prices playing a catch-up across most of the states in the

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · DHIRAJ KAPOOR
chunks.text:
down during August, but we have seen prices playing a catch-up across most of the states in the
Eastern corridor since early October. South have been the strongest momentum in prices, volume
and capacity utilization. South markets are transforming. Mark my words. You might remember
something which I had spoken to you a few quarters ago about the Southern markets. North held

steady, new prices have been absorbed, while Central has played a muted game. Into October,
we are seeing continuous increase in prices. The festive weeks may slow down and how quickly
these prices are absorbed, so we expect the full benefit of these price increases to reflect in the
Q3 earnings rather than immediately. So that’s about prices.
Three points stand out. Realizations in the previous quarter were essentially stable. So, prices
were not the cause of any decline in performance. Fuel costs and raw material costs rose about
13% and 3% quarter-on-quarter. Fuel costs have risen from INR45 a bag to INR51.5 per bag.
That is the contribution of fuel cost Y-o-Y as the fuel rates climbed to about INR2.09 per kcal.
This is the West Asia crisis effect, which we can discuss separately. Third, other fixed costs per
ton were 6% lower for us than the last year, even after absorbing new capacity because absolute

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · DHIRAJ KAPOOR
chunks.text:
ton were 6% lower for us than the last year, even after absorbing new capacity because absolute
fixed costs grew only 4%, well below the volume growth of 13.8%. This is the operating leverage
working for UltraTech as intended. September month has given a glimpse of what comes next,
that is an internal number. But as volumes remain strong, price increases have been coming
through, when we look month-to-month performance, September was higher than the Q2
average.
Let me get to the next element of our industry, which is demand. Industry estimates put cement
demand to grow closer to 10% year-on-year. Our growth of 13.8% this quarter is comfortably
ahead, which means that our presence in the market is continuously increasing. North markets
grew in high double digits. We have grown more than 20% in the Northern markets, in the range
of 15% to 20% in the Southern markets, East around 5%, West around closer to 10% as well as
10% in the Central markets. Our capacity utilization was 71%, better than 66% last year on a
higher base. We could have grown more. We could have sold more cement if additional capacity
was available. And that's why we are excited about our next phase of growth. which is around
the corner. Capacity utilization, people often ask me, let me give you the numbers upfront. North
and South, both were upwards of 70%. West was a close second to about 70%, Central and East

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · DHIRAJ KAPOOR
chunks.text:
and South, both were upwards of 70%. West was a close second to about 70%, Central and East
because of prolonged and heavy monsoons in the Eastern markets, till 2 or 3 days ago also I
believe West Bengal was raining. That's why the capacity utilizations were a shade around 60%.
This quarter, we have commissioned a greenfield cement capacity in the Southern markets.
Demand is growing in South, prices are improving, and we are in a happy place in the Southern
markets.
Housing markets, individual homebuilder markets, the backbone of retail demand kept buying
through the quarter, helped by fewer rain lost days. Public capex, Central government capex was
very strong through July, though road construction has been weak. However, we are seeing new
awards have picked up, which will result into higher demand in the following quarters or in the
next couple of years. The project pipeline keeps growing. I believe there were 100
announcements worth about INR13.4 lakh crores by early September, which include Tamil
Nadu's INR55,000 crores power plant, INR65,000 crores Gorakhpur Industrial Park, Assam's
INR50,000 crores 5-year infra program, Odisha's Coastal Highway, Metro 1 in
Thiruvananthapuram and the Bawal-Behror RRTS, power, industrial parks, data centres, all are
growing and all are cement intensive. In the state of Bihar, West Bengal, we are waiting for

growing and all are cement intensive. In the state of Bihar, West Bengal, we are waiting for
demand to unleash. There are multiple projects in pipeline, which will boost capacity utilization
for us in the Eastern corridor as well.

Looking ahead, most estimates put industry should grow very strong. We expect to grow
stronger, supported by our capacity addition and market reach. Activity typically picks up mid-
November or as you are all aware, after what is called Chhath Puja, after all the festive season
is over and monsoons out of the way completely. We have already seen good signs of strong
momentum in demand. Much talked about monsoons, let me not shy away from that. Monsoons
were very weak this year since 2015. And I guess I'm told it's the fourth lowest since 2001. But
India has seen 4 very good preceding years with good monsoons, which is a very positive sign.
There are drought situations in some part of the country, which I'm sure you're all aware of. How
does it impact us? Fewer rain loss days kept sites working and made the usual seasonal dip in
volumes much lower. This is one of the reasons why industry would be growing very close to
10%, which is in a quarter which is normally a weaker quarter. East was the exception because

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · DHIRAJ KAPOOR
chunks.text:
10%, which is in a quarter which is normally a weaker quarter. East was the exception because
East had torrential rains, local spells in July and August, heavy rains, flooding disrupted
construction and pulled down both volumes and prices in that region. Weak monsoon can hurt
farm incomes and, with a lag, rural housing. But an important point to keep in mind is that Indian
economy has been evolving. There are several non-crop activities, which are contributing to
almost 40% of rural economy with the help of MSME, non-agri sectors growing, mushrooming
everywhere in the country. Besides, as I mentioned, last 4 years of good monsoons will also help
or act as a cushion. We expect rural demand might soften in some areas, while urban housing,
infrastructure, private sector capex will continue to grow very strongly.
West Asia crisis, last quarter, we were expecting a deescalation, crude prices falling and things
becoming normal, but a candid acceptance from my end, predicting a roll of a dice is easier than
what will be the outcome on the West Asia crisis. How it is impacting us? Pet coke prices have
shot through the roof. They were trading around $180 per ton as I last checked. Pet coke, what
we have done is we have reduced our dependence on pet coke since the last quarter. Today, we
are down to about 25% of pet coke consumption in our overall mix. Coal power plants are being

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · DHIRAJ KAPOOR
chunks.text:
are down to about 25% of pet coke consumption in our overall mix. Coal power plants are being
required to blend imported coal. Coal India is giving priority to the power sector, which tightens
the domestic availability for the industry. Industrial diesel prices have been continuously
increased by the government. I believe they are at an all-time high as we speak, which impacts
the raw material costs vis-a-vis the mining cost or the transportation costs.
These cost pressures, as we speak, we don't know what will happen, as I mentioned, about the
West Asia crisis, are here for some more time. That's all I can imagine. So far, we have not seen
any direct impact on cement demand. Our volumes show that clearly. The indirect risks are
higher inflation, tighter monetary conditions and less fiscal room if fuel does not come down in
terms of costs. We are watching all the 3 elements. Our response follows a strategic plan, price
discipline, product mix and premium products and relentless cost work across fuel sourcing,
power and logistics.
Our growth plans is the next topic, which I want to touch upon. We commissioned 4.6 million
tons of capacity in the month of September, taking our domestic cement capacity to 204.7 million
tons, which includes the 3.6 million tons greenfield capacity at Petnikota in Andhra and 1 million

ton of debottlenecking at 3 other units. During the quarter, we also added 116 megawatts of
renewable power, 10 megawatt of waste heat recovery. So our green power index keeps on
rising, 47% of our power needs were met from non-fossil fuel sources. We have also achieved a

sector. We have commissioned AFR systems at 2 plants, taking our thermal substitution rate to
about 7.2%. We are on track to reach 240 million tons of capacity as planned without any
surprises.
Ultravolt - On 3rd September this year, we launched our Wires and Cables business under the
brand Ultravolt. We already have a huge channel partner force in place. The investment of
INR1,800 crores, which has been planned, we have spent around INR1,100 crores till date and
the balance will get spent in the next maybe 2 quarters. This is the first month of launch or first

patience, we will deliver an electrifying performance. UltraTech has helped build walls, and
now we are getting behind the walls. We have started with wires and light-duty cables. It appears

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · DHIRAJ KAPOOR
chunks.text:
now we are getting behind the walls. We have started with wires and light-duty cables. It appears
to be a very exciting space, and we are confident of growing rapidly. Currently, dealers,
distributors, retailers, builders, contractors, electricians are all EPC firms and panel builders are
all getting on board. More than 1,500 UltraTech UBS channel partners have signed up to become
dealers for our Ultravolt as a brand. Our retail reach has already crossed about 80,000 points and
growing very rapidly. Supply chain is in place. We have a mother plant at Jhagadia in Gujarat,
1 main warehouse with 5 regional distribution centres and 16-odd branch warehouses.
Production and sales of house wire, panel wire and multicore cable has already started.
Remaining power and control cable lines will be commissioned through the second half. Our
focus for this quarter shifts from building the network to stabilizing it. That means consistent fill
rate at the counter reliable replenishment from warehouse dealers, credit discipline, tracking of
secondary sales. The aim is that every new partner sees the business turnover steadily, not just
onetime launch. We are building this business. Our performance will speak.
To sum up, cement is our core. We are growing very strongly in cement. And as I alluded to, we
are looking forward to our next phase of growth, which will take us way beyond 240 million

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · DHIRAJ KAPOOR
chunks.text:
are looking forward to our next phase of growth, which will take us way beyond 240 million
tons of capacity. Cement demand is resilient, and we shall keep growing very strong. Prices have
held through the monsoons are turning up at the exit and seem to be holding. Cost remains a
challenge whilst West Asia situation unfold on an everyday basis.
We are entering now the strongest season of the year with a better price run rate, more capacity
and cost structure that improves with scale. I won't pretend that second half will be free of cost
pressures. What I can promise is that we will manage it much better than anybody else under the
sun. And you will see similar performance from UltraTech quarter after quarter.
Thank you, as always, for trust in UltraTech, and over to you for questions.

− Infrastructure demand grew as project execution picked up ahead of the elections.
